title: Hershele, Rabbi for a Day
summary: The grand Squire races into Mezhibozh with four hard questions and threatens to take the pond and all the geese if no one can answer. But Rabbi Baruch has gone to visit a sick man! So Hershele Ostropoler puts on the Rabbi's enormous fur hat and takes his chair. A funny rhyming story with a repeating line that is fun to shout together.
pages:
Into town came the Squire, his carriage racing fast,
a feather in his hat and a face like a stormy blast.
"Fetch me the Rabbi! Four hard questions I bring!
If no one can answer — I'll take your pond and your geese, every last thing!"

The Hasidim whispered: "The Rabbi's not here! He's gone to visit the sick!
Who will answer the Squire now? Oy, what trouble! Think quick!"

Hershele smiled: "I'll answer for him, my friends — don't you fear!
Just lend me the Rabbi's fur hat — for two hours, right here!"
The hat was so huge, it came down over his eyes,
and he shuffled to the chair, hardly seeing his feet — what a size!

"You — the Rabbi?" asked the Squire, suspicious and stern.
"Yes," said Hershele, pushing the hat back. "Ask, sir — but please wait your turn!"

"Question one! How many stars are in the sky?"
"As many as the hairs in your horse's tail! Count them one by one, with both hands — give it a try!"
And if you don't believe it — go and check!

"Question two! How long does it take to go around the world? A year?"
"Just one day! Simply run after the sun — it goes all the way round, and never stops anywhere, my dear!"
And if you don't believe it — go and check!

"Question three! What am I thinking right now? Just guess — no questions, if you please!"
"You think you're talking to the Rabbi — but I'm Hershele, and his hat is only borrowed, you see!"
And if you don't believe it — go and check!

"Question four! Which is heavier: a kilo of feathers or a kilo of stones?"
"They're both a kilo! But try putting the stones on your head — and see the face you make, with moans and groans!"
And if you don't believe it — go and check!

The Squire laughed, stood up, put a hand on his heart, and sighed:
"The pond stays here, and the geese stay too — right there, side by side!"
He climbed into his carriage, his feather shaking with laughter, nonstop,
and off the horses galloped — clop, clop, clop!

Back came the Rabbi from the sick man, and there was his hat on Hershele, who'd sunk inside it like a pea in a pot.
"Well?" he asked. And from inside the hat: "Four questions, four answers — and the Squire left with his storm forgot!"

That night the Rabbi gazed at the stars and asked softly: "How many are up there in the sky?"
And Hershele smiled: "As many as the hairs in a horse's tail — count them with both hands, give it a try!"
And if you don't believe it — go and check!
